traits.flowering_months.note: iNaturalist research-grade records on GBIF in the south and central Puget Sound lowlands (46.7 to 48.0° N, 122.0 to 123.1° W; counted 2026-10-14): 427 records annotated as flowering (May 1, Jun 128, Jul 186, Aug 70, Sep 24, Oct 17, Dec 1); stated as the months holding at least a tenth of them, June to August. FEIS (Chamerion angustifolium) gives June to September across the range.

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS (Chamerion angustifolium): fruits mature about a month after the flowers and release their seed from August; with its flowers here from June to August, its capsules are ripe from August to October.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as Epilobium angustifolium: stems 50 cm to 2.5 m tall. The typical value is the one the plant was drawn at before, inside the source's range.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as Epilobium angustifolium: leaves 5 cm to 15 cm (to 20 cm) long.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a spreading clone of unbranched stems 1 to 2 m tall with many narrow, willow-like leaves in a spiral, and a long terminal raceme that opens from the bottom, with seed pods below the open flowers and nodding buds at the tip. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated. Each plant draws its height within the 0.5 to 2.5 m Abrams gives its stems, so the tolerance spans that range.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: four broad magenta petals with a pale centre, deep pink buds, red-purple seed pods and reddish stems.

taxon.note: Common name (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

taxon.scientific_name.note: WCVP v16's accepted name for the plant the spec's authors wrote as Chamaenerion angustifolium, which WCVP treats as a synonym.

taxon.genus.note: The genus WCVP v16's accepted name is written in.

traits.note: The Flora of North America's account of the species, as quoted in search results (the page itself was not read): inflorescences erect racemes, 5 to 50 cm.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Abrams's Illustrated Flora of the Pacific States, volume 3 (1951), Onagraceae by P. A. Munz: fireweed's leaves are alternate, unlike most willow-herbs, whose lower leaves are opposite; the Myrtales' usual opposite leaves do not hold for it.

appearance.organs.flower.note: Its raceme drawn as one cluster that opens by the day (spec rework L1c), its kind from its characters, by the rule at the flowering plants, where before the herb placed flowers, buds and capsules along the stem by their place, whatever the day: 40 flowers, by eye (the Fire Effects Information System says 15 or more; long racemes bear more), on a raceme about 45 cm long, each flower about 2.6 cm across with four magenta petals (2 to 3 cm), from deep pink buds, and slender capsules 6.5 cm long after, drawn twice as thick as in life, the thinnest fruit a fruit look draws. Its tip bends over 20 degrees, set by hand over its erect posture, for the buds that nod there (Jepson: nodding in bud). From floras and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read. The plant stands as tall as before: its stems end where the raceme begins.

appearance.organs.flower.season.note: Its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall come from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were set by eye: its days by eye from the months floras give for flowering (the Fire Effects Information System: June through September), for lowland plants: buds in mid-June, each flower open about 10 days, the raceme opening from its foot over about 50 days (floras and guides say it opens from the bottom up, and give no time), its capsules split and its seeds shed by mid-October.

appearance.organs.flower.season.flower_l.note: Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5): four petals, four sepals, eight stamens and a pistil of four carpels on an inferior ovary, from the characters of the Onagraceae by the rules at the flowering plants. By hand, from Minnesota Wildflowers and Minnesota Seasons (as search results quote them; the pages themselves were not read): the long, slender, purplish ovary behind the flower that looks like a short stalk, about one and a half times the flower's radius; the sepals about half as long as the petals, the same colour but darker.
